As part of what has now become a daily ritual, Raghu Bharvad greets Swamishri in a corner of the pradakshina, and lovingly says: "Bapa! Now that I have had your darshan, I feel there is nothing left for me to see or do."

Swamishri humbly acknowledged Raghu's sentiments, and then remarked: "In the time of Shriji Maharaj, there was Jodho Bharvad [of Gadhada]. Here [in Sarangpur], there was Hajo Bharvad. Now, we have you!"

Suresh is an exuberant youth from Botad. He descends from a devout and dedicated family that has served most sincerely since the times of Shastriji Maharaj.

Today, Suresh is holding a tamburo - a single-stringed musical instrument. As Swamishri comes, he starts plucking away and mumbling 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan'' He then offers the tamburo to Swamishri, gesturing him to do the same. Swamishri complies graciously, and begins to pluck the instrument and chant 'Swaminarayan' Swaminarayan''
On his way out of the Rang Mandap, Swamishri sees Suresh seated with the tamburo, and smilingly acknowledges this simple youth's devotion.
